subject: Memory Exhausted Error for Latent Interaction Model

messages.author: 1efa3b71e04ef2d9
messages.subject: Memory Exhausted Error for Latent Interaction Model
parts:
Hi All,

Has anyone ever run into the error message: "Error: memory exhausted (limit reached?)" before? I fit a model that included some latent interactions using data with just over 600 observations with some missing data. The model took about 10 hours to fit using the sem() command, so I'm guessing I'm running close to the memory limit. The model is also several hundred lines long, but I'm happy to post any part of the code that might be helpful in solving this issue since I know this is incredibly vague.

The model itself on the original data worked well, but then I simulated sample data using the simulateData() command and parameters from the original data. When I tried running this simulated data using the original lavaan model (for a power analysis, so ideally I'll do this thousands of times), I got the error message. Nothing is different except the data. Is there an obvious thing I'm doing wrong?

Thank you,
Jessica

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Memory Exhausted Error for Latent Interaction Model
parts: I fit a model that included some latent interactions using data with just over 600 observations with some missing data.
Multiple latent interactions, using product indicators?  Sounds like a complex model for only 600 observations.  How many variables, including product indicators?
The model itself on the original data worked well
What does that mean?  A model without interactions / product indicators?

but then I simulated sample data using the simulateData() command and parameters from the original data. When I tried running this simulated data using the original lavaan model (for a power analysis, so ideally I'll do this thousands of times), I got the error message. Nothing is different except the data. Is there an obvious thing I'm doing wrong?

Simulations can take a long time.  Are you saying it took 10 hours to fit (or get an error?) the model to a single simulated sample?  If you simulated data from a model without latent interactions, then calculated product indicators and tried to model latent interactions, then you are trying to estimate lots of parameters that are really zero, which could make the optimizer wander around looking for a solution.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Memory Exhausted Error for Latent Interaction Model
parts: Thank you both so much for the helpful suggestions! Apologies for just now seeing this and replying.

I fit a model that included some latent interactions using data with just over 600 observations with some missing data. 

Multiple latent interactions, using product indicators?  Sounds like a complex model for only 600 observations.  How many variables, including product indicators?

Exactly, multiple latent interactions using product indicators, based on the Kenny & Judd (1984) approach. It is a pretty complex model but suggested by reviewers so we tried it and made it clear that it was exploratory. Four variables (PROCESS Model 14 if we used OLS if that helps). The antecedent variable has 9 indicators, the first mediator has 4 indicators, the second serial mediator has 7 indicators, the moderator has 12 indicators, and the outcome variable has 32 indicators.

The model itself on the original data worked well

What does that mean?  A model without interactions / product indicators?

I was able to write syntax and it fit the model and gave estimates on the actual data we collected. The model had all the interactions and product indicators (which was amazing, thank you for all the functionality of lavaan). The problem happened when I wanted to run this same model on simulated samples of data. So the only change was using simulated data from simulateData() instead of the original data. Same model with all indicators and interactions.

but then I simulated sample data using the simulateData() command and parameters from the original data. When I tried running this simulated data using the original lavaan model (for a power analysis, so ideally I'll do this thousands of times), I got the error message. Nothing is different except the data. Is there an obvious thing I'm doing wrong?

Simulations can take a long time.  Are you saying it took 10 hours to fit (or get an error?) the model to a single simulated sample?  If you simulated data from a model without latent interactions, then calculated product indicators and tried to model latent interactions, then you are trying to estimate lots of parameters that are really zero, which could make the optimizer wander around looking for a solution.

That makes sense, and you're right it took 10 hours to fit with the collected data and 10 hours to give the error using simulated data. Interesting point about trying to estimate lots of parameters that are really zero. I simulated data from a model that included the interaction though in the structural model, along with the measurement model including all the product indicators. Is it possible that's just too many parameters for only 600 observations?

Thank you!
Jessica
